<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, touching **85** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/index.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**5** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/objects.mdx`  _(via tenant_id (literal, a string literal in AMENDMENT_COLUMNS; a string literal in CHECKPOINT_COLUMNS))_
- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via tenant_id (literal, a string literal in AMENDMENT_COLUMNS; a string literal in CHECKPOINT_COLUMNS), os audit verify (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/audit/verify.ts))_
- `content/docs/deployment/seed-tenancy-repair.mdx`  _(via tenant_id (literal, a string literal in AMENDMENT_COLUMNS; a string literal in CHECKPOINT_COLUMNS))_
- `content/docs/permissions/record-view-auditing.mdx`  _(via tenant_id (literal, a string literal in AMENDMENT_COLUMNS; a string literal in CHECKPOINT_COLUMNS))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/config-resolution.mdx`  _(via tenant_id (literal, a string literal in AMENDMENT_COLUMNS; a string literal in CHECKPOINT_COLUMNS))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/implementation-status.mdx`  _(via tenant_id (literal, a string literal in AMENDMENT_COLUMNS; a string literal in CHECKPOINT_COLUMNS))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via tenant_id (literal, a string literal in AMENDMENT_COLUMNS; a string literal in CHECKPOINT_COLUMNS))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via tenant_id (literal, a string literal in AMENDMENT_COLUMNS; a string literal in CHECKPOINT_COLUMNS))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/index.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **27** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **44** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 463b8ea5d223bb20e25350303b7bee19217375ac` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `884306361ec0a6040508e3e930468fb9d89df578` — the merge of head `f92faa38eacad50464999b3efa2f155e28d1cfd7` into base `463b8ea5d223bb20e25350303b7bee19217375ac`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 884306361ec0a6040508e3e930468fb9d89df578 && git checkout 884306361ec0a6040508e3e930468fb9d89df578
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 463b8ea5d223bb20e25350303b7bee19217375ac f92faa38eacad50464999b3efa2f155e28d1cfd7 && git checkout -B drift-repro 463b8ea5d223bb20e25350303b7bee19217375ac && git merge --no-ff f92faa38eacad50464999b3efa2f155e28d1cfd7

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 463b8ea5d223bb20e25350303b7bee19217375ac
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 463b8ea5d223bb20e25350303b7bee19217375ac` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Contract review of #32508 · 2026-11-12T02:30Z (CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER sub-agent run by the seat, adopted by the seat)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `c9cd4603aa41f60fec6551ab64c5872fa11356b9`
Local-runs: none

Face: declaration (`Clause-②: yes (widening)` on the PR body and in the changeset). The file list has no governed path and no `packages/spec/**` path, and the `Governed Surface Queue Guard` check-run passed.

Check-runs on this head at 2026-11-12T02:27Z: 0 failed and 15 skipped (path-scheduled or opt-in). Every other completed run passed, including Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Lint · ESLint, Lint & Repo Gates, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, PR-body guards, Spec property liveness, Type Check · source gates and debt ledger, Build Docs, Dogfood Regression Gate, Live E2E UI and Test UI. **Not finished:** Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Build Core, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · consumer gates. Landing waits for these.

### ① Derived judgments

- **CLI flags: right.** `--out FILE`, `--bundle FILE` and `--trusted-key FINGERPRINT` (repeatable) are additions. These usage errors exit 2 (`usage`):
  - `--bundle` without `--trusted-key`;
  - `--trusted-key` without `--bundle`;
  - `--bundle` with `--out`;
  - `--bundle` with `--database-url` given on the command line;
  - `--bundle` with `--org`, `--from` or `--to`;
  - a `--trusted-key` that is not 64 hex digits (trimmed and lowercased first).

  D9 states this exactly: "`--bundle` is mutually exclusive with `--out` and with booting… any other combination is refused as a usage error". `bundle_unreadable`, `bundle_invalid` and `bundle_write_failed` also exit 2, which is right because no verdict is given. Offline, the run exits 0 or 1 as the live run does.
- **New exports: right.** The package exports only its root (`exports["."]`). The root gains `verifyAuditProofBundle`, `AuditProofBundleError`, `AUDIT_PROOF_BUNDLE_FORMAT` and the type `AuditProofBundle`. `AuditVerifyOptions` gains the optional `onProofBundle`, and the bundle is built only when it is passed. No export is removed or retyped.
  - `VerdictLedger`, `ChainCheck`, `judgingOrder` and `CheckpointHead` are `@internal` and are not exported from the barrel.
  - `AUDIT_PROOF_BUNDLE_FORMAT` has no consumer outside the package. That matches the precedent of `AUDIT_ROW_VERDICTS`, and ruling (f) of 6795974647 names it.
  - `AuditProofBundleError` is not in ruling (f); see ③.
- **Bundle content against D9: right.**
  - `keys` holds only the keys the live anchor vouched for, as raw public halves with their fingerprints.
  - Every in-scope checkpoint is carried whatever `--from` / `--to` say: its signed body, `id`, `chain_key`, `signature` and `leaf_hashes`. A row that is not a signed body is copied column by column.
  - Every in-scope amendment is carried, and so are the live run's unsealed rows.
  - `leaves` come from `leafInput`: the clear columns in canonical form, and each value column only as `commitValue(salt, …)`. A row in neither store is `null`, and a value with no canonical spelling is `'unreadable'`.
  - `seed_handle` is a `sys_secret` row id, not a seed. The bundle holds no value, salt or seed. A byte scan in the plugin test pins this (values, wrapped secrets, opened seeds, column salts), and the CLI spawn test scans the written file the same way.
- **One verdict machine: right.** Signatures, D8 honouring, links and the D7 row judgment live in `VerdictLedger` and `ChainCheck`. The live and offline checks differ only in where records, leaf inputs and keys come from.
  - Offline, a key is used only when its fingerprint is in `trustedKeys` AND the bundle's 32-byte, canonical-base64 half hashes to it.
  - D8 is judged at the offline check's own time, not at the bundle's `checked_at`.
  - `verifyNow` asserts offline equals live, fault texts and `checked_at` aside, in all 34 earlier scenarios.
  - The one input not re-derived offline is the unsealed list, which is carried as the writing run's statement. D9 provides for this: "It cannot re-read the rows; that is what the live run that wrote the bundle did."
- **`trustedSigningKey` / `trustedPublicKey`: right.** The `sys_secret` read now happens outside the catch, so a read fault throws. In the live check, `publicKeyOf` still turns a missing table (`sys_audit_signing_key` or `sys_secret`) into "untrusted" and rethrows any other fault, which the CLI reports as `verify_failed`, exit 2.
  - A missing half (`!handle`), a half that does not open, or one that derives another key still returns `null`.
  - Pins: a read fault rejects the run (new); a corrupted ciphertext reads untrusted and the run fails (new); a missing half reads `null` (existing signer pin).
  - The `IAuditCheckpointSigner.trustedPublicKey` contract ("`null` when it vouches for none") still holds.
- **Deviation, `--bundle` refuses `--org`, `--from` and `--to`: right.** This is D9's "any other combination" rule. The bundle's scope is fixed by the `--out` run, and the refusal says to scope that run instead.
- **Deviation, no dangling redaction listed for a row with an unreadable value: right.** D7 lists a dangling amendment for a row that reads `unmodified`. Such a row read `modified` on `main` too: the override on column B never rescued an unreadable column A, because `leafInput` still threw on A. `dangling` does not enter `ok`, so the verdict is unchanged.
- **should-fix S1.** `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx` and the `--out` flag help leave out D9's bullet "A bundle carries personal data". The clear columns (`user_id`, `actor`, `ip_address`, `user_agent`, `tenant_id`) identify people. The bundle is to be handled as a ledger export and narrowed with `--org` / `--from` / `--to`. The help's "(never a value, salt or seed)" reads as safe to hand out. Not blocking, because the content matches D9. Fix in a follow-up on this PR or carry to P3.
- **nit n1.** `writeFile(…, { mode: 0o600 })` sets the mode only when it creates the file. An existing file is overwritten and keeps its old mode.
- **nit n2.** The CLI spawn tier pins three of the seven usage errors. `--bundle` with `--org`, `--from`, `--to` or `--database-url`, and a malformed `--trusted-key`, have no CLI pin. The plugin tier pins the non-fingerprint case.
- **nit n3.** The missing-`sys_secret`-table case at the anchor now depends on `publicKeyOf`'s classifier instead of a swallowed catch, and has no pin.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/plugin-audit` and `@objectstack/cli` is right. AGENTS.md (Post-Task Checklist, step 3) says the level follows the `Metadata-protocol` kind alone: `none` takes `patch`, and "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch`".
- The new flags and exports are a non-protocol widening, so `patch`.
- A store read fault while opening a key now exits 2 instead of 1. That is a non-protocol change on an error path: no input `main` accepts is refused, and a run that gave a false tamper verdict now gives no verdict. So `patch`. Check Changeset passed.

`Clause-②: yes (widening)` is truthful. The diff only adds; no export, flag or accepted input is removed or refused. The parenthetical names the new flags and exports and discloses the exit-code change. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: no authorable key, `lifecycle.seal` is unchanged, and no spec path is touched.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `patch`, not `minor`: answered in ②.
- `--bundle` refusing scope flags: accepted (①).
- `$OS_DATABASE_URL` alone ignored with `--bundle`: accepted. An environment value is not a combination the operator gave.
- `onProofBundle`, a name beside ruling (f): accepted. It is an optional, additive option.
- **Not flagged by the dev:** `AuditProofBundleError` is a new root export that is neither in ruling (f) nor among the recorded deviations. The name is right: the CLI needs it to tell "no verdict" (exit 2) from a verdict (exit 1). This record ratifies it for the seat.
- Bundle built in memory, its size growing with the judged range: accepted for stage 1, since `--from` / `--to` bound it. Stays visible beside S7.
- Dangling redaction: accepted (①).
- Unsealed rows carried as the live run's statement, and tail truncation leaving no gap: accepted. These are D9's "cannot re-read the rows" and the ADR's "Truncating a chain's head is not detectable on the host" (stage 2). Both are stated in `bundle.ts` and the docs.
- `main` moved three commits with no file overlap, not merged: accepted.
- `open_questions`: none.
- Out-of-scope (class c): a crypto provider whose `decrypt` faults transiently still reads as an untrusted key. **Escalated:** the seat carries it on #31908 beside S9, with `carrier: cloud` for a KMS provider. It needs a provider-level fault class and is not this slice's work.
- `security_findings`: one low-severity note, routed privately to the security seat; it does not block this PR.
- The S9 sealer error line does not touch `--bundle`, which boots nothing.

Delta contract review of #32508 · 2026-11-12T03:13Z (TIER_DEFAULT sub-agent run by the seat, adopted by the seat; answers 6812632692)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `f92faa38eacad50464999b3efa2f155e28d1cfd7`
Local-runs: none
Scope: DELTA `c9cd4603aa41f60fec6551ab64c5872fa11356b9`..head (one commit, `f92faa38`, 5 files, +51 −14)

Face: declaration (`Clause-②: yes (widening)` on the PR body and in the changeset). The delta touches no governed path and no `packages/spec/**` path. Inputs: the earlier record on this PR (head `c9cd4603`), the delta, the PR body at head, ADR-0154 D9, and the check-runs on this head.

Check-runs on this head at review time: 56 in all, 0 failed, 38 passed and 17 skipped (path-scheduled or opt-in). Passed runs include Build Core, Build Docs, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint · ESLint, Lint & Repo Gates, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, PR-body guards, Spec property liveness, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Dogfood Regression Gate, Live E2E UI, Test UI, and Test Core 2/8 to 8/8. **Not finished:** Test Core (1/8). Landing waits for it.

### ① Derived judgments

- **S1 (personal data): answered, and truthful in all five places.** D9 says: "A bundle carries personal data. Its clear columns (`user_id`, `actor`, `ip_address`, `user_agent`, `tenant_id`) identify people. It is an export of the ledger and is handled as one … and narrowed with `--org` / `--from` / `--to`."
  - The `--out` flag help now says the bundle is an export of the ledger, carries personal data, is handled as the ledger and is narrowed with the scope flags. It drops "(never a value, salt or seed)", which read as safe to hand out, and keeps "commitments; no salt or seed".
  - The new human line after an `--out` write names user, actor, IP address, user agent and organization. These are the five D9 columns. `tenant_id` is a lookup to `sys_organization`, so "organization" is correct.
  - `cli.mdx` changes the `--out` bullet and adds a "**A bundle carries personal data.**" paragraph. It quotes D9's five columns and its handling and narrowing rule, and adds that the file is written with mode `0600`. That statement is true: see n1.
  - The `AuditProofBundle` type doc and the `verify.ts` class jsdoc both say a bundle is an export of the ledger, handled as one (D9).
  - The changeset says the same and adds `0600`.
- **The new warning is not a contract-surface change.** It is `printWarning`, which writes to **stdout** through `console.log`, the same as the `printSuccess` line before it and the file's other human-mode warnings. It is printed only on the human path after `--out`. The `--json` branch emits and returns before it, so the JSON document and stdout purity do not change. Exit codes do not change: the line is printed before `this.exit(1)` on a failing verdict.
- **n1 (`0600` on overwrite): fixed.** `writeFile(…, { mode: 0o600 })` is now followed by `chmod(out, 0o600)`, so a file that already exists is narrowed too. Test 5 writes a `0644` file at the `--out` path first and asserts `statSync(...).mode & 0o777 === 0o600`. The PR body reports ablation 13 (the `chmod` removed) as red. If `chmod` throws, the shared catch refuses with `bundle_write_failed` and exit 2. No verdict exit is given, which fails closed. See nit n4 for that path.
- **n2 (usage-error spawn pins): fixed, and the pins assert what they claim.** Test 7 adds three runs. Each one trips exactly one rule, and each asserts exit 2, `error: 'usage'` and its own message:
  - `scoped` passes `--org`, `--from` and `--to` together. The message lists the flags it found, and the regex requires `--org, --from, --to`. Dropping any one of the three from the filter would therefore turn the pin red, so the three are pinned separately in effect. The dates are valid ISO and the date parse runs after the `--bundle` block, so no other refusal can answer first.
  - `withDatabaseUrl` gives `--database-url` on the command line, with nothing else wrong.
  - `badKey` gives one malformed key, so it passes the "at least one key" check and fails the fingerprint check.
- **`$OS_DATABASE_URL` in the right-fingerprint run: proves the point.** `childEnv` strips `OS_DATABASE_URL` and its siblings from the parent environment, so only the `rightHuman` run sets it. The flag declares `env: 'OS_DATABASE_URL'`, so oclif fills `flags['database-url']` from the environment. The refusal is keyed on `this.argv` (`given('database-url')`), not on the parsed value. If that check read the parsed value, `rightHuman` would exit 2 and its `code === 0` and "verifies" assertions would turn red. So the run proves that the variable alone is not a usage error.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/plugin-audit` and `@objectstack/cli` still holds. The delta adds no export, flag or accepted input. It changes text, a human-mode stdout line, the file mode of an `--out` file, and tests. `--out` does not exist on `main`, so its new `chmod` failure path refuses nothing that `main` accepts. Check Changeset passed.

`Clause-② (widening)` still describes the diff truthfully: "new flags and new exports; nothing main accepts is refused, and a store read fault while opening a signing key now ends the run with exit 2". The delta neither adds to nor contradicts it. `Metadata-protocol: none` stands.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Earlier note, `AuditProofBundleError`: answered.** The PR body now lists it under Recorded deviations as "Ratified at contract review", which matches the earlier record.
- **Earlier nit n3 (no pin for a missing `sys_secret` table at the anchor): not addressed in the delta.** The delta does not touch the plugin tests. It stays open as a nit.
- **nit n4 (new): `chmod` failure after a successful write.** If `writeFile` succeeds and `chmod` then fails (for example `EPERM` on a writable file another user owns), the bundle is on disk with its old, wider mode. The refusal says it "could not be written", which is inaccurate. Either of two fixes would narrow the mode before any content lands and make the message true:
  - write to a temporary file created `0600`, then rename it over the target;
  - remove the existing file, then create it.

  The same fix would close the window between `writeFile` and `chmod`, during which an overwritten file holds the new content under its old mode. Not blocking: the `--out` path is chosen by the operator.
- **nit n5 (new): the human `--out` warning has no pin.** `cleanHuman` does not pass `--out`, so no test asserts the personal-data line.
- **nit n6 (new): `never-opened.db` is not checked.** The `rightHuman` run names the database file `never-opened.db`, but no assertion checks that the file is still absent afterwards.
- **`main`: no overlap.** `main` moved 12 commits past the merge base `7d13a333`. None touches this PR's 10 files, ADR-0154, `plugin-audit`, `commands/audit` or `utils/format.ts`. Not merging is accepted.
- **Claims not re-run here.** The PR body's ablations 13 to 16 and its gate and suite results on `f92faa38` are the dev's claims. They were read, not re-run (read-only).
- `open_questions`: none.

Seat record: ACCEPT #32508 · 2026-11-12T03:17Z · head `f92faa38eacad50464999b3efa2f155e28d1cfd7`

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：`os audit verify` 新增离线证明包：`--out FILE` 在在线校验时把公钥、检查点、修正记录和叶子输入（值列只存承诺）写成一个包；`--bundle FILE --trusted-key 指纹` 不连库就能复核，判定和在线校验用同一套机器。另外修了打开签名密钥时 `sys_secret` 读失败被当成「密钥不可信」的问题，现在退出码 2（不给判定）。
- 为什么改：ADR-0154 D9 要求审计账本能交给外部审计方离线复核（#31908 的 P2b 部分）。
- 风险与回滚：只新增 CLI 参数和 `plugin-audit` 的导出（`Clause-②: yes (widening)`），两个包 patch；主线已接受的输入都不拒。证明包含个人数据（用户、操作者、IP、UA、组织），帮助、文档和写出后的提示都写明了，文件权限 0600。回滚即还原本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/bundle.ts`；`packages/cli/src/commands/audit/verify.ts` 的 `--out` / `--bundle` 分支。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli exec vitest run src/commands/audit/verify.integration.test.ts`，12/12 通过。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地（落地动作若再被分类器拦下，会挂 `pm:awaiting-merge` 等人转 ready）。

席位意见：ACCEPT。按 step-0 裁定（6795974647，P2a 在线 / P2b 证明包拆分）实现。TIER_DEFAULT 评审 PASS（6812632692），补丁轮增量复审 PASS（本 PR 上紧接其后的 delta 记录）。
